statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk is low on a contained, two-sided overnight Nasdaq-100 range, while Stress is elevated on firm crude, the highest 10-year yield since January 2025 and an unresolved US-Iran escalation.
recommendation: Conditions are consistent with the mapped EA_ON state for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Tail remains well below the block threshold because no persistent one-way structure is observed. The narrow danger window covers the 13:30-15:00 UTC US cash open and the 14:00 UTC ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases, where whipsaw potential is concentrated.
headline: Contained overnight Nasdaq-100 range against firm crude and the highest 10-year yield since January 2025
body: NQ futures trade near 29,489, about -0.1%, inside a roughly 90-point overnight range with repeated two-sided rotation and no observed directional efficiency. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Monday at 29,456.97, up 0.08%, off the session low of 29,304.49 and outperforming the S&P 500 at -0.33% and the Dow at -0.70%. The cross-asset backdrop is materially risk-negative: US forces struck Iranian launchers in the Strait of Hormuz and Iran fired ballistic missiles at US bases in Jordan, lifting Brent above $91 and WTI to roughly $87, while the 10-year Treasury yield reached about 4.76%, the highest since January 2025, and September Fed hike pricing moved to roughly 62-65%. VIX at 14.92 remains low in absolute terms. This is a conflict between an inflation and rates channel that is clearly risk-negative and an index tape that has so far absorbed it, which maps to elevated Stress rather than elevated Tail. The pathological no-retracement path that would overwhelm a mean-reversion approach is not in evidence: pullbacks are occurring, the overnight range is narrow, and NQ is not holding a session extreme. The principal unresolved amplifier is geopolitical discontinuity out of the Strait of Hormuz, which is a gap channel rather than an observed structure. The nearest scheduled checkpoints are the US cash open at 13:30 UTC and ISM Manufacturing with JOLTS at 14:00 UTC. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read but was approximately 216 minutes old at assessment time, beyond the 90-minute freshness bound, so it was treated as stale and not used materially; independent primary-source research carried the assessment.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 hours the published Claude assessment stayed continuously in the EA_ON band, with Tail between 5 and 17 and Stress drifting from the high 30s into the mid 50s. The one Tail peak at 17 came in the 09:00 UTC hour on August 31 during a European event/whipsaw window. From the US session onward Stress climbed steadily as crude extended and the 10-year yield pushed to its highest level since January 2025, while Tail stayed in single digits to low teens because retracements kept occurring and no one-way structure developed. Dominant mode was mixed for 22 of the 24 hours.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is continued contained, two-sided trade with an elevated-Stress, low-Tail profile. Conditional risk concentrates in a narrow band around the 13:30 UTC US cash open and the 14:00 UTC ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases, where forecast Tail peaks at 18 and dominant mode is projected as event/whipsaw, still below the block band. Risk is projected to decay through the US afternoon and normalise after the 20:00 UTC cash close. The standing invalidation risks are a Strait of Hormuz disruption headline producing an oil-driven gap, and a further hawkish repricing of the September Fed decision. Forecast Confidence declines from 87 to 70 across the horizon.
